lead.h1: Mexico's state-owned electricity utility to rely on private sector for investment funding
lead.context: Mexico's state-owned electricity utility will depend on the private sector to finance most of its investments during President Sheinbaum's term.
lead.background: Mexico's state-owned electricity utility plans US$37.5 billion for new power plants, grids and pipelines. Reliable connections to the national grid are already a constraint on new industrial projects.
lead.view: The financing structure matters as much as the total. Keeping projects off Mexico's state-owned electricity utility's balance sheet may protect its financial position, but private funding alone does not establish that a plant or transmission line will be built.
lead.prediction: Watch which projects obtain signed financing and construction schedules. Those milestones would confirm that the plan is becoming usable electricity capacity, while repeated delays would weaken that conclusion.

items.headline: Mexico exports reach record 80 billion dollars in July 2026
items.context: Mexican exports surpassed 80 billion dollars in July, with imports also at record levels driven by demand for intermediate goods.
items.background: Mexico sends about 80% of its exports to the United States, so a national export record is also a measure of Mexico's exposure to one foreign market.
items.view: Compared with June, July exports rose about 12.3%. Imports also reached a record because firms bought more intermediate goods, so the headline does not show how much of the final value was created in Mexico.
items.prediction: The next monthly trade release will show whether July was a one-off jump. If exports and intermediate-goods imports remain high together, the record will look more like sustained factory activity than a temporary surge.
